purpose: Pre-registered confirmation plan: v6-v11 (and the v10/v12 reviewer-response extensions) all selected methods, arms, comparisons and seeds on the SAME validation split, so their p-values are exploratory. This manifest freezes the main comparisons, endpoints, seed count and statistics BEFORE any WikiText-103 test-split evaluation, and the confirmation data (wiki.test.raw) has never been read by any earlier phase. v2 (review-2 revision): the seed count was raised 6 -> 12 and the manifest gained a machine-checkable binding block and a scope declaration; the revision was made strictly BEFORE any test-split evaluation (no P5T result has ever existed -- no results_lm_test/ record, no commit touching the test split), which is the only condition under which a pre-registration may be revised without selection bias. v3 (review-3 revision, 2026-10-19): aligned the stamp with CODE_SEMANTICS v11.128, corrected the implementation binding (all four frozen arms run the per-row RoPE loop, so eager_batch=false is the TRUTH), pinned the per-arm mlp_ratio, disclosed the parameter-vs-compute mismatch and the changed decision rule, and added a zero-GPU plan self-check. Again strictly BEFORE any test-split access.
implementation_binding_note: v11.128: eager_batch is FALSE for every frozen arm. All four arms have rope=True, and HybridAttentionRoPE.forward routes every CSA layer through the per-row _single_rope loop; csa_kernels has no RoPE/qk-norm batched twin. The old v2 value (true) certified a batched path that never ran for csa_fixed_rope / _allblocks and simultaneously rejected randidx / full_rope. amp_dtype=bf16 requires an Ampere-or-newer GPU (exp_lib._active_amp now refuses bf16 on pre-Ampere cards instead of silently changing the numerical path); amp_grad_scaler is false for bf16.
implementation_binding_provenance: predicted by exp_lib._uses_batched_eager + make_layer_cfgs and checked against every P5T record's real train_knobs; `python v12_supp.py plan` exercises the same admission path on synthetic records WITHOUT reading test data.
training_recipe: P3MT/P4MT/P5C: 3000 steps, seq 512, batch 12 (18.4M tokens consumed per run over the 8M-token train cache; identical data order per seed), all four arms under one config; csa_fixed_rope & full_rope via P3MT/P4MT (seeds 0-5) + P5C (seeds 6-11), controls via P3MTC/P5C (seeds 0-11, same recipe and outdir).

binding.training_recipe_note: Machine-checkable subset of the run_cfg fingerprint (keys as decoded by exp_lib.run_cfg_knobs). mt/det/df/cs are deliberately NOT pinned: they bind variant/environment/data/code and are verified separately (_code stamp, data_fp, manifest sha). v3 pins the parameter-matching knob mr per arm (binding.per_arm_recipe_signature): the shared signature cannot express one value for four arms because full_rope must be widened to mr=6.76348876953125 while the three csa arms stay at mr=4. Any record whose recipe fails this signature (including the per-arm mr) is refused by the confirmation statistics entry.

training_data_fingerprint.fingerprint_rule: exp_lib._ids_fp over the served 1-D train ids (train_fp on every checkpoint and training record)
training_data_fingerprint.binding_rule: if canonical_train_fp is a non-null string, every checkpoint and every admissible record must match it; otherwise all frozen checkpoints/records must agree on ONE non-null train_fp, which the first P5T access writes into results_lm_test/.freeze_lock.json and every later run must match. Mixed or missing train_fp is a hard refusal.
training_data_fingerprint.note: The literal value is intentionally not guessed here: it becomes checkable only against a built wt103_cache. Until then the run derives it from the frozen checkpoints BEFORE the first test read and locks it; a later change of training corpus is rejected.

test_slice.fingerprint_rule: exp_lib._ids_fp over the flattened (n_seqs, seq_len) rows; every record must carry the same non-null data_fp; the first P5T access writes it into results_lm_test/.freeze_lock.json

tokenizer.fit: same deterministic BPE fit as load_wikitext (first <=50k TRAIN rows only, vocab 8192)
tokenizer.check: load_wikitest hard-compares the full id->token vocabulary against the cached train tokenizer AND the persisted tokenizer bytes (sha256 recorded in test_meta) on every cache hit; a mismatch is a hard refusal, not a warning

checkpoint.stamp: v11.128 (= exp_lib.CODE_SEMANTICS; records carry _code, ckpt carries code)
checkpoint.hash: sha256 of the .pt file, stored per record as ckpt_sha256 at P5T evaluation time

eval.data: wiki.test.raw via exp_lib.load_wikitest (held out; the ONLY phase allowed to read it)
eval.per_document: bylen records additionally store ppl_per_seq (per-row PPL) so document-sampling uncertainty can be stratified; n_seqs=16 does NOT cover the language-population distribution and population-level claims are out of scope (design_notes section 20)

scope.confirmatory_claims: ONLY fixed-chunk CSA mechanism claims: learned top-k selection vs trained controls, sparse length extrapolation vs full RoPE attention, and block-compression/KV-projection effects at the frozen endpoints.
scope.not_covered: dynamic chunking vs fixed chunking, semantic value of dynamic boundaries, HCA advantages, and dynamic-chunking scaling laws are NOT covered by this confirmation (no dynamic arm, no HCA comparison is frozen here).
scope.required_for: those claims require their own pre-registered freeze (arms, seeds, endpoints) before their first test-split access; until then they stay exploratory regardless of how the fixed-chunk confirmation turns out.

compute_budget_disclosure.parameter_matching: full_rope is param-matched to csa_fixed_rope by widening its MLP to mr=6.76348876953125 (hand check: total params A=C=D=11,089,904 vs B=11,088,512, 0.013% apart). This is capacity reallocation, not compute matching.
compute_budget_disclosure.flops: per-token training FLOPs of the dense reference are about 1.87x the csa arm (2.30M vs 1.23M: MLP +69%, attention 3.2x at L512).
compute_budget_disclosure.read_fraction: learned csa reads 32/128 = 25% of blocks at train L512 and 32/1024 = 3.1% at eval L4096; dense reads 100%; allblocks reads 128 blocks at L512 and 1024 at L4096.
compute_budget_disclosure.kernel: csa arms use the manual _rope_attn path (explicit -inf mask + split softmax); full_rope uses SDPA and switches backend between bf16 training and fp32 eval.
compute_budget_disclosure.reporting_rule: REPORT_v12.md and any paper table must state these caveats next to the comparison names; do not describe the main comparison as 'sparse vs dense at equal compute'.

primary_comparisons.name: main: csa_fixed_rope - full_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: csa_fixed_rope better (negative delta) would confirm the sparse length-extrapolation advantage seen on validation
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: NOT a single-factor contrast. The dense reference is parameter-matched by widening its MLP to mr=6.76348876953125 (hidden 1731 vs 1024, +69% MLP width); per-token training FLOPs are therefore ~1.87x the csa arm (MLP +69%, attention 3.2x at L512). csa_fixed_rope reads 32/128 blocks at train L512 (25%) and 32/1024 at eval L4096 (3.1%), while full_rope reads 100%. The comparison also changes the attention kernel (manual _rope_attn vs SDPA), q_norm (extra F.normalize), kv_norm width (256 vs 32) and the learned sink (full_rope has full_sink=False). Report all four differences, not just 'parameter-matched dense'.

primary_comparisons.name: control: csa_fixed_rope_randidx - csa_fixed_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: positive delta would confirm that learned selection beats a TRAINED random selector at equal budget (the test-time intervention cannot answer this)
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: 'random' is a FIXED deterministic hash pattern ((row*12.9898 + col*78.233)), identical for every seed, layer and step — not a fresh random draw. The claim is about learned selection vs this fixed pseudo-random read pattern, at matched parameters (but with 201,216 dead W_DQ/W_DK/W_w parameters in the randidx arm, so its effective parameter count is ~1.8% lower).

primary_comparisons.name: control: csa_fixed_rope_allblocks - csa_fixed_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: positive delta would confirm that learned top-32 selection beats TRAINED all-block reading (allblocks reads strictly more information; this is a selection-vs-full-read contrast, NOT an equal-budget contrast)
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v3 CORRECTS the v2 'at equal budget' wording: the arms are parameter-matched but NOT computation/reading-budget matched. index_topk=1000000, and lightning_indexer internally caps k=min(topk, B): allblocks reads 128 blocks at train L512 and 1024 blocks at eval L4096, versus 32 for learned (about 32x more at L4096). It is therefore an information-rich 'read everything' control, which is scientifically valid but must not be described as equal budget. The indexer's STE soft prior also differs (log(1/32) vs log(1/1024) on the selected set), so the learned sink strength differs by about 30x at L4096; 'only index_topk changed' is not accurate.

primary_comparisons.name: aligned-dense: full_rope - csa_fixed_rope_allblocks @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: isolates block-compression/KV-projection from selection: same-projection dense-style reading vs standard dense attention (non-directional mechanism readout)
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: Not a single-factor contrast either: full_rope uses SDPA (bf16 in training, fp32 in eval — a backend switch), no learned sink, kv_norm width 256, and an extra F.normalize(q); the csa arm uses the manual _rope_attn kernel with a sink and kv_norm 32. Kernel/reduction-order differences are part of the measured delta.

statistics.test: exact two-sided sign-flip over paired per-seed deltas
statistics.min_seeds_note: v3 pre-registers that a comparison may be CONFIRMED with fewer than the 12 frozen seeds when at least 8 complete pairs remain. Rationale: with a two-sided exact sign-flip and Holm/4, 8 seeds are the smallest n whose minimum attainable Holm p (4*2/2^8 = 0.03125) is below alpha=0.05. The old code required all 12 seeds via coverage_ok, so one failed L4096 cell annihilated an otherwise complete comparison; v3 drops only the incomplete pair, reports the actual n_effective, and applies this declared floor.
statistics.min_consistency_note: v3 clarifies that 11 is a SUFFICIENT condition under the equal-magnitude symbol-test projection, NOT the minimum for the exact sign-flip test. For unequal |delta| the exact test can reject with 8/12 same-sign (e.g. 8x(+100) and 4x(-1): exact p=0.0078, Holm p=0.031). It is recorded for reference and is not used as a decision threshold.
statistics.power_note: q = probability that a single seed's paired delta falls in the pre-registered direction. The table is computed by exp_lib.signflip_power, which implements the SYMBOL-TEST projection 2*P(Bin(n,1/2) <= n-k), NOT the exact sign-flip test that finaltest_stats actually runs. It is neither a design guarantee nor a rigorous bound in either direction: for unequal magnitudes the exact test can be more powerful (8/12 can suffice), and it can be less powerful when contrary deltas are large. Use it only as a rough design aid. Before the first test access, simulate sign-flips on the P5C per-seed validation delta vector (fixed |d_i|, enumerate 2^12 sign patterns) to obtain the real power / minimum same-sign count for THIS panel; if that power is inadequate, add seeds and record the revision in revision.history BEFORE touching test.
statistics.validity_assumptions: the exact sign-flip p requires within-seed exchangeability: both arms of a pair share everything stochastic except the arm itself (identical per-seed data order over the shared cache, same eval rows, same corruption grid; init RNG is seeded per seed -- architecture-induced RNG consumption differences are part of the arm). Seed-number equality alone does not provide this; see design_notes section 20. Machine-checked: data_fp, train_fp, n_seq, recipe, _code, manifest sha. Reported but NOT enforced: rng_fp (analysis writes validity.rng_fp_values / same_rng_fp).
statistics.decision_rule: A comparison is CONFIRMED only if p_holm < 0.05 AND its direction matches the validation-panel estimate AND param_matched is not false AND at least min_seeds_for_confirmation=8 complete pairs entered the test. coverage_ok (all 12 seeds) is reported but is not required. Otherwise the claim stays exploratory. Probe/delta-NLL/NIAH results on the test split are reported descriptively (secondary) and carry no significance claims.
statistics.seed_policy: seeds 0-11 fixed above; no seeds may be added after the first test-split evaluation (adding seeds after seeing results is selection bias by construction). Missing or incomplete seeds are reported as-is (smaller honest n_effective, never topped up); the declared floor is 8 complete pairs. The load-time power gate refuses any future manifest whose min attainable Holm p at that floor exceeds alpha.
